note: v1 95.76 (seeds 0/11 95.76/94.59), Late for the Grid: warped boom-bap off a worn sampler at 84 bpm. Nothing sits on the grid: the lofi-kit's kick a hair early, the snare lazy-late, the hats swung and scattered, under rolled tape-piano chords (Fm9 Abmaj9 | Eb6/9 Dbmaj9 | Fm9 Bbm11 | C7#9 C7b9), a late gliding analog bass, a wobbly boc-lead hook and vinyl crackle; a straight dotted-eighth shaker runs against the swing. The drift grows through the song (A3 widest), bars trip short and catch themselves, the master dips into the break, and the last chorus snaps back near the grid. Drafts 79 -> 95.8: EQ to the lo-fi envelope (cut 215 Hz, air above 6 kHz), the shaker for off-grid periodicity, two-stage compression for the lo-fi loudness.

v2 95.46 (seed 0; v1 re-scored 95.54): a real TAPE-STOP into the break. The master's tapestop fx is held for the two beats before the break by an automation lane, so the whole beat - kit, piano, bass, hook - slows and sags to a halt (the window just before the break differs from v1 by -14 dB re its level) and the break's piano and bass start clean after it. Measured, not heard: the effect is placed, Harry's ear decides.

v3 96.30 (seeds 0/11 96.30/95.37 vs v2 re-scored 94.62/93.51; pin 232211dd): wM's new lo-fi toolkit on the two voices that carry the song. The rolled tape-piano chords now go through a warbling TAPE DECK (wow 12 cents, flutter 2.5, a seeded drift, the top end darkening in the speed dips), so the chords bend and sag as they ring; the kit goes through SP-1200-style 12-bit sampling (crush at 26 kHz, half wet), so the drums alias like an old sampler. Tried and dropped this round: the tape deck and vinyl fx on the whole master (and in place of the crackle track) smoothed the song into four sections and lost its returns (recurrence 100 -> 19, 78); a second tape-stop bar before the last chorus did not bring them back.

v4 96.43 (seeds 0/11 96.43/96.16 vs v3 re-scored 96.41/95.49): THE GLITCH, after Harry's note on chirper-three's glitch resample. Every TRIP bar (the bars cut short, five of them) is now also a sampler glitch: the master's stutter fx (sixteenth slices, three repeats, decaying, seeded) opens for the tripped bar's second half only, so the beat stumbles AND skips like a sampler losing its place, then catches itself on the next downbeat. The trips used to be heard only as missing time; now they are events (the glitch window differs from v3 by about its own level).

v5 97.11 (seeds 0/11 97.11/97.42 vs v4 96.43/96.16): Late for the Grid gets a FORM and a proper mix. (1) THE LIFT: the second groove and the last chorus move the whole loop up a fourth (Bbm9 Dbmaj9 | Ab6/9 Gbmaj9 | Bbm9 Ebm11 | F7#9 F7b9), hook and bass with them, so the song now has a key to rise to and come home from. (2) THE REPRISE: after the tape-stop break the first groove returns exactly as it began (no hook) before A3's widest drift. Form: intro | A | A2 (lift) | break | A reprise | A3 | last (lift, snapped tight) | outro - the song stopped reading as two long blocks (its sections were 4-5 and its returns flipped with every mix change; now 5-6 on both seeds). (3) The mix against the lo-fi envelope: weight at 45 Hz instead of a cut at 52, the 225 Hz box cut deeper, 400 Hz and 1.9 kHz down, 1 kHz up.
rebaselined on compscore 78004071: v5 (the song file) scores 93.920/93.714 on seeds 0/11; best was 97.11 on an older compscore. Compare candidates against this.

v6 96.74 (seeds 0/11 96.74/96.74 vs v5 rebaselined 93.92/93.71): SECTION COLOURS - Late for the Grid's form is finally heard the same way every time. The intro and the outro now play the rolled loop on a warbling wurli (the song's bookends; the tape piano carries everything between them), and the first lift (A2) voices the loop an octave higher. Every turn of the form gets its own colour, so compscore finds the same six sections on both seeds (it found 3 to 6 before, and every mix change flipped its returns): variety 83 -> 100 (timbre spread 2.7 -> 8.2 dB), returns steady. Voicing the last chorus up an octave too made it a copy of A2 (recurrence share .75, 92.1).

v7 96.74 (seeds 0/11 96.74/96.74, level with v6): THE CHOPS, at last. Three times the sampler chops in the break broke compscore's reading of the form; with v6's section colours the form holds, so the break now gets them: after the tape-stop, an MPC-style chop of the library's lofihop part re-sequenced over the break's piano and bass (slices in orders the original never played - 0 0 5 3 0 7 6 2, a doubled 9, a doubled 13 - in swung eighths). The break is now the producer's moment: the beat stops, the tape sags, and a flipped sample talks over the bass before the groove comes back.

v8 96.84 (seeds 0/11 96.84/96.84 vs v7 re-scored 96.83/96.83; pin 7adf6cd2): SNARE THROWS, the dub move, with chirper-two's feedback routing. On every fourth bar of the grooves the beat-3 snare is doubled on a throw track sent into a dub bus whose own output returns a dotted sixteenth later through a 1.8 kHz low-pass and a wobbling tape, 6 dB down each pass - the producer's hand slapping the send, so each phrase ends with a snare echo tumbling, darkening and sagging into the next. Levels found by test: a hotter loop (send 0, return -4, limiter -6 dB) became a constant howl that sank the whole mix (81-82); wM's epiano-reed for the bookend wurli cost variety (96.09).
